professional: a behavioural-biometrics / bot-detection researcher who reviews mouse-dynamics papers (e.g. for Pattern Recognition, IEEE TIFS, USENIX Security); first checks: does the pipeline reproduce from the released data, are people split so the detector is scored on unseen users, is the closest prior work on synthetic mouse trajectories and mouse-dynamics bot detection cited (Chu et al. 2013 'Blog or block'; Acien et al. 2022 BeCAPTCHA-Mouse, Pattern Recognition 127; Antal et al. 2021 SapiAgent, IEEE Access), is the detector anywhere near the state of the art, is the copying guard sound, and are 8-seed effects stated with honest intervals.

evidence.correctness: Ran the pipeline on a private copy (/tmp/claude-0/audit-mimic-cursor/w1): report.py regenerates results.txt and results/crossplay.json byte-identically (24 s), experiments/figure.py regenerates figure.svg identically, baselines.py reproduces every row of section I (3 m 45 s), and run.one(('blind',0,30)) reproduces results/run_blind_0.json exactly (identical JSON, 2 m 19 s). Independent script scripts/indep.py (no subject import) recomputes from the run JSONs: 960 rounds, 40 below loop AUROC 0.6, min 0.0037, 23 of 39 rebound above 0.8, reference min 0.8205 (README 'never below 0.82'), final means 0.996/1.000/0.988/0.989, own bootstrap (20,000 resamples, different RNG) intervals within 0.003 of results.txt, component counts 13/22/24/25 of 32, cross-play row means 0.699/0.741/0.777/0.811 and paired strength +0.042/+0.078/+0.112 (-0.005 to 0.248), ceiling 1000 evaluations = 8.3x the game's 120. Against outside standards: Fitts duration in Shannon form (MacKenzie 1992) a=250,b=120,D=400,W=20 gives 777.1 ms, generator ends at 777; minimum-jerk position (Flash and Hogan 1985) at tau=0.25 and 0.5 is 103.516 and 500.0 of 1000 px, generator gives the same; five feature functions match hand values on a toy stroke; all 7,695 stored strokes satisfy data.py's stated segmentation rules (>=8 points, chord >=40 px, <=3000 ms, no gap >250 ms, t0=0) and there are 46 sessions (10 v0 + 36 v1) as claimed. Not 4: the raw DUX files could not be fetched (zenodo.org 403 through the proxy), so strokes.json.gz was not rebuilt from source; ceiling.py (about 40 min) was not rerun.
evidence.completeness: Claimed items checked: 9 tests (ran 9, pass, 6.7 s); results.txt, crossplay.json, figure.svg regenerate identically; baselines.json reproduces; a full 30-round run reproduces bit-for-bit; data.py rebuild and ceiling.py not rerun (download blocked, runtime). All four conditions, the reference detector, cross-play, the copy test and the ceiling are implemented as described. No stubs or TODOs. Runtime 'about 40 minutes on 4 CPUs' for run.py is conservative (one run 2.3 min, so about 19 min for 32 runs on 4 workers here). Live page https://marisstella.app/research/mimic-cursor/ returned 000 from this container (not verified).
evidence.verification: `/usr/bin/python3.13 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 9 pass. quality_mutate.py, 6 seeded mutants, 1 caught: disabling the copy cap in the imitator's evaluation (game.py:125, > MAX_COPY -> > 10*MAX_COPY), wrong minimum-jerk coefficients (programs.py:115), the detector swapping its strongest instead of weakest feature (game.py:102), the d2i imitator targeting the smallest shared gap (game.py:134) and the fractional-coordinate feature any->all (programs.py:264) all survive; only a 2x change to the copy-test ratio (game.py:72) is caught. report.py, which computes every published interval and the cross-play matrix, has no test at all. The tests check shapes, budgets and endpoints, not any published number or any rule that decides who wins the game.
evidence.craft: Read data.py, game.py, programs.py, run.py, baselines.py, ceiling.py, report.py, tests/test_cursor.py, experiments/figure.py. Small, readable modules with docstrings that state the method; deterministic seeding throughout (verified by exact reproduction). Defects: module-level mutable globals (game.COPY, programs.HUMAN) must be set by the caller before anything works, and the tests monkeypatch module functions to count calls; the calibration comment above MAX_COPY (game.py:31-33: 6.8%, 9.3%, 89%, 39%) disagrees with the shipped baselines (6.4%, 7.4%, 91.7%, 42.7%); report.py opens files without closing them; figure.py depends on research/_shared/linefig.py (fine, but undeclared in the README's dependency list).
evidence.claims: Every number in the README Result and Results sections is in results.txt and recomputes from results/ (checked rows above). Limits are stated at length (one form, 46 people, 8 seeds, component library chosen by the authors, 3-of-11 feature restriction, templates as few-shot examples), plus guardrails and a no-affiliation line. Weak points: 'Copy rates on held-out contexts stay at 0.07 to 0.11' (per-run final copy rates are 0.048 to 0.114; condition means 0.073 to 0.083); the mechanism 'rotating a trajectory breaks the screen-axis pixel quantisation ... heading-change and pixel-step features see it' is an explanation with no ablation file behind it; 'all intervals including 0' is true only at the boundary for d2i (0.000 to 0.010).
evidence.fitness: A researcher could build on it: the game, detectors and per-round JSON reproduce exactly, and mimic-codeloop already does. As a contribution it is preliminary and largely negative (feedback does not change who wins; the both-ways detector advantage +0.112 has an interval including 0 at 8 seeds). The nearest prior work is not cited: synthetic mouse-trajectory generation against bot detectors (Acien et al. 2022 BeCAPTCHA-Mouse, function-based and GAN trajectories, near-perfect detection, the same headline 'kinematic models are easy to catch'), SapiAgent (Antal, Buza and Fejer 2021, an autoencoder bot evaluated against mouse-dynamics detectors), and Chu et al. 2013's behavioural-biometrics bot detection. The feedback-channel comparison is new framing, but a reviewer would ask how the headline differs from BeCAPTCHA-Mouse and why the detector is a 3-feature logistic regression.
evidence.domain: Sound in its basics (split by person, held-out reference detector, Fitts and minimum-jerk components implemented correctly). Departures a mouse-dynamics reviewer would raise: detectors are hand-feature logistic regression and gradient boosting, not the sequence models used in current mouse-dynamics bot detection, so 'fooled' is narrow (stated); strokes are pause-cut movement runs, not aimed movements, so Fitts' law with a guessed W=20 has little to bite on (stated); the copy test is a nearest-neighbour ratio, not Meehan et al.'s three-sample Mann-Whitney test, and compares a template bank of 3,845 strokes with a reference bank of 1,012, so the bank-size asymmetry alone biases the ratio toward 'copy' (held-out people score 6.4%; calibrated empirically, but not a property of the method); all 8 seeds share one data split (rng 12345) and one reference/test set, so intervals cover game randomness only, not which people were held out.

defects.what: Core game rules are untested: switching off the copy cap in the imitator's evaluation (game.py:125), the detector's feature-swap rule (game.py:102), the d2i targeting rule (game.py:134), the minimum-jerk profile (programs.py:115) and the fractional-pixel feature (programs.py:264) can all be broken with every test green (5 of 6 mutants survive). The copy cap is the guard that keeps the imitator from replaying training data; nothing fails if it stops applying. report.py, which computes every published interval and the cross-play matrix, has no test.

Prior work on synthetic mouse trajectories against bot detectors is not cited: BeCAPTCHA-Mouse (Acien et al. 2022) already reports function-based and GAN trajectories detected near-perfectly, SapiAgent (Antal et al. 2021) is a learned human-like mouse bot, Chu et al. (2013) is the behavioural-biometrics bot detector baseline. A reader cannot tell what this adds beyond the feedback-channel framing.

Copy test departs from the cited method: a nearest-neighbour distance ratio (twice as close to the template bank as to unseen people) instead of Meehan et al.'s three-sample test, with a 3,845-stroke template bank against a 1,012-stroke reference bank, so bank size alone pushes the ratio toward 'copy' (held-out people already score 6.4%, a straight-line bot 7.4%). Calibrated empirically, but described as 'after Meehan et al. 2020' without the departure.

All seeds share one data split and one reference/test set (split() rng 12345, fixed_sets rng 777), so the bootstrap intervals cover game randomness only, not which 16 people were held out; with 8 seeds a percentile bootstrap also runs narrow.
Calibration comment for MAX_COPY quotes 6.8% / 9.3% / 89% / 39%, but the shipped baselines give 6.4% / 7.4% / 91.7% / 42.7%.

'Copy rates on held-out contexts stay at 0.07 to 0.11' understates the spread: per-run final copy rates run 0.048 to 0.114 (the condition means are 0.073 to 0.083); and the pixel-quantisation explanation for the replay baseline has no ablation file behind it.

Module-level mutable globals (game.COPY, programs.HUMAN) must be filled by the caller before generate/copy_rate work; forgetting setup_copy/set_human fails late with a NoneType error, and the tests depend on monkeypatching module functions.

verdict: A well-built, exactly reproducible stylised study: report.py, figure.py and baselines.py regenerate their outputs byte-for-byte, a full 30-round run reproduces its stored JSON exactly, and an independent script recomputes every headline count, mean, bootstrap interval and cross-play mean from the per-run data; the Fitts and minimum-jerk components match their textbook forms. Claims are honest and heavily limited, with small imprecisions (copy-rate range, a stale calibration comment). It misses the bar on verification: 5 of 6 seeded bugs in core game logic survive, including switching off the copy cap, and report.py is untested. As research it is a preliminary negative result at 8 seeds that does not cite the closest mouse-trajectory bot literature (BeCAPTCHA-Mouse, SapiAgent, Chu et al.), uses a copy test that departs from the method it cites, and puts every seed on one data split. Correct and finished, not yet what a mouse-dynamics reviewer would accept as a contribution.
